contracts.purpose: Identify the user's main continuous activity and protect its workspace, position, and shortest interaction path.
contracts.trigger: Every meaningful web workspace, dashboard, editor, form, control panel, or browser-interface decision.
simple_rules: Identify the user's main continuous activity before allocating the screen.
Give the primary task the best position, most useful space, and shortest path.
Keep frequent support reachable without covering the work field.
Move setup and maintenance outside the continuous work field.
Fail when secondary panels or status compress the primary task.
Verify the protected work field with real content at target sizes.
On an orientation homepage, expose one dominant decision or next action and keep alternate paths contextual.

contracts.purpose: Classify web-interface information by operational importance and avoid permanent equal-weight display.
contracts.trigger: Before arranging labels, data, help, status, setup, maintenance, or diagnostics in a web interface.
simple_rules: Classify each item as CRITICAL, PRIMARY, SUPPORTING, CONTEXTUAL, SETUP, or MAINTENANCE.
Do not display every class permanently or with equal visual weight.
Keep PRIMARY information continuously available for the current task.
Show CRITICAL information immediately but only when it is truly critical.
Reveal CONTEXTUAL, SETUP, and MAINTENANCE information at the relevant moment.
Place technical detail below the user result unless the audience needs it continuously.
Promote missing information that blocks progress above routine summaries and normal status.
Keep healthy routine system state visually quiet and expose technical setup contextually unless it changes the current decision.

contracts.purpose: Define the real user flow before implementing isolated screens or static mockups.
contracts.trigger: Before implementing a new screen, route, modal, form, dashboard, or multi-step web interaction.
simple_rules: Record entry, goal, decisions, primary action, feedback, result, and next destination.
Do not implement an isolated screen without its workflow context.
Keep required decisions close to the action they affect.
Make feedback describe what changed and what happens next.
Preserve task continuity across routes, dialogs, and responsive modes.
Test the flow from entry through result with real interaction.
Use one understandable navigation hierarchy for the current surface; duplicate mechanisms must not compete.

contracts.purpose: Validate web layouts and interactions with realistic, missing, long, nested, multilingual, and extreme content.
contracts.trigger: During implementation and before accepting any web layout, component, list, table, editor, or data view.
simple_rules: Test long names, messages, labels, and unbroken values.
Test empty values, errors, and missing assets.
Test large lists and nested structures without idealized truncation.
Test different languages and unusually large and small values.
Preserve meaning when content wraps, truncates, scrolls, or expands.
Reject layouts that pass only with ideal demo content.

contracts.purpose: Implement and verify the relevant default, pointer, keyboard, progress, outcome, and empty interaction states.
contracts.trigger: Every interactive web control, form, asynchronous action, collection, and task outcome.
simple_rules: Implement DEFAULT, HOVER, FOCUS, ACTIVE, and DISABLED where applicable.
Implement LOADING, SUCCESS, ERROR, and EMPTY where applicable.
Make focus visible and preserve keyboard task completion.
Do not use color as the only state signal.
Keep disabled and loading controls understandable and non-destructive.
Verify real state transitions instead of accepting a static mockup.
A meaningful FAILED state names the plain-language cause, user consequence, and corrective action without exposing secrets.

contracts.purpose: Preserve completion of the primary task across narrow, standard, and wide browser workspaces.
contracts.trigger: Every web layout or component whose available width, height, scaling, or input mode can change.
simple_rules: Define what remains visible, collapses, moves, and becomes contextual.
Declare what must never be hidden for task completion.
Use wide displays to improve work, not merely stretch line length.
Preserve the primary action and result on narrow displays.
Avoid overlaying essential controls or content at any target size.
Verify narrow and wide modes in a real browser with realistic content.

contracts.purpose: Control hierarchy, grouping, density, spacing, contrast, and competing accents for the actual audience and task.
contracts.trigger: During visual composition and after functional structure and information priority are known.
simple_rules: Use hierarchy and grouping to make the primary task and decisions legible.
Choose density for the audience and task instead of enforcing minimalism.
Accept dense professional interfaces when density supports fast precise work.
Use spacing consistently to express relationships, not decoration.
Limit competing accents and preserve sufficient contrast.
Apply visual refinement only after purpose, structure, content, and states work.

contracts.purpose: Inspect the real implemented interface in severity order, fix hard failures, and preserve strengths before polish.
contracts.trigger: After the interface runs in a browser and before any completion or acceptance claim.
simple_rules: Review hard failures before primary-task and information-architecture blockers.
Then review interaction, responsive, accessibility, and visual failures.
Record strengths to preserve only after failures are identified.
Fix hard failures before optional visual polish.
Repeat browser inspection and screenshots after corrections.
Block completion when lens, browser, state, responsive, screenshot, or QA evidence is missing.
